Head-sha: `2555c75f77ac6e6287f4715cbb68ce501d91576e`

Read against claim 6963059050 and card #34597. The change is 3 files, +25/-2, all inside the surface: `rules/aggregation.md`, one eval case under `skills/objectstack-query/evals/`, and a root changeset.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- **The rewritten parenthetical matches the code at this head.**
  - `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` ~1455–1458 decides the pushdown: `zoneNative = kind === 'utc' || (kind === 'area' && drv.supports.zonedDateBucketing === true)`.
  - `judgeBucketZone` (~1580–1589) classes a resolved zone that contains `/` as `area`, and anything else as `memory`. So `Asia/Taipei` pushes down, while `+08:00` and `EST5EDT` stay in memory on every driver. Those are the same examples the code comment uses.
  - `sql-driver.ts:409` declares `zonedDateBucketing: this.isPostgres`. "PostgreSQL via `driver-sql`" is exact.
  - The unchanged first half also still holds: a granularity the driver does not bucket natively stays in memory, by `allStructuredSupported`.
- **The eval case is consistent with the rule.**
  - Its expected answer (PostgreSQL in the database, SQLite in memory, `+08:00` in memory everywhere) is what the code does. `aggregationFilter` is declared by `driver-sql`, so the filtered count rides the PostgreSQL pushdown.
  - The `must_not_contain` targets the code spelling `timezone: '+08:00'`, not the prose mention.
  - The JSON parses.
- **No other stale sentence.** A grep of the query skill finds no other claim that a zoned bucket always stays in memory. `SKILL.md`:43 only says `aggregate` reads `timezone` itself.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2555c75f77ac6e6287f4715cbb68ce501d91576e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-query/evals/filters-pagination-search.json, skills/objectstack-query/rules/aggregation.md + none
Security-touching: no

Inputs read: card #34597 body and all four comments (triage 6936606127, 6939907025; claim 6963059050; os-dev-report 6963493632), PR #35012 body, its three-file list, the net diff against `main` (merge-base `4443014630`), and the check-runs on the head. The diff holds no file that implements or enforces the two `hits` (no code, no gate), so the `+` side is `none`; the engine and driver were read at the head, not reviewed. The changeset is the lane seat's remainder.

### ① Derived judgments

- Public surface: one published skill sentence (`rules/aggregation.md`, the FILTER WHERE note's parenthetical) and one published eval case (id 9). No schema, no accept-set, no code path, no generated artefact changes. Right: the card asks for exactly this sentence and "keep or add" an eval case.
- The sentence widens what the skill promises on PostgreSQL (a zoned bucket in the database) and keeps the old promise everywhere else. That matches the merged engine, so it is a correction of text to behaviour, not a behaviour change. Right.
- File surface matches the claim (two skill files plus a root changeset); nothing in `packages/**`. Right.
- Check-runs on the head, read at review time: every completed run is `success` or `skipped`, including `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`. Four were still `in_progress` and carry no verdict yet: `Test Core (1/10)`, `Test Core (2/10)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`. This record does not vouch for those four; the seat reads them before landing. The token-ratchet figure (2346 of 2357) is the dev's reading; the gate family that holds it completed `success`, and the figure itself was not re-run here.
- The skill-eval runner (`packages/qa/scenarios`, `skill-evals`) is by its own README not a CI job and not a merge gate, so no check-run answers whether case 9 passes against a model. The dev's script check proves only that `expected_output` satisfies its own tokens. The card's Done-when ("the skill eval for it passes") is therefore unmeasured on this head; see S1.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/34597-skills-zoned-date-bucket.md` declares `@objectstack/skills` patch, the same shape as earlier skills-text changesets on `main` (for example `33565-retried-callout-in-subflow-skill.md`). Published text only, no API or schema: patch is right. `Check Changeset` completed `success`.

Clause-②: no — on the PR body and in the changeset, and correct: the diff changes no runtime behaviour, removes nothing and narrows nothing. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct for the same reason. The changeset's prose agrees with the tree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions` 1 (authored at `TIER_DEFAULT` while `dispatch-gates --tier` mandates the contract-review tier for `skills/**`): answered by this record, which is the at-tier review of the authored text (the dev's option A). Whether an at-tier review cures an under-tier authoring run is the seat's call under its own ruling; nothing in the diff argues against A, since the text is five lines and every clause was checked against code below.
- Dev out-of-scope finding (`content/docs/data-modeling/queries.mdx` says the SQL driver ignores a structured `groupBy` alias while the skill says column keys are correct either way): outside both `hits` and outside the diff. Not judged here; "noted, not filed" leaves a possible docs-versus-skill contradiction without a carrier, so the seat should file it or state why not.
- Dev deviation (model-free commit trailer instead of the harness reminder's): process, not contract; left to the seat.
- Author: PR `user.login` was not read as a separate field; the body is relay-signed by the dev session. Nothing to add.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no code in the diff, so no new id materialisation or in-app join. The text itself moves in the SQL-first direction: it stops telling authors that a zoned bucket is always an in-memory call.

### ④ Design judgment

**`skills/objectstack-query/rules/aggregation.md`**, clause by clause against `packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` and `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts` at the head:

- "a date bucket the driver does not bucket natively keeps the whole call in memory" — true. `allStructuredSupported` reads `supports.queryDateGranularity[g]`, and `nativeAggregate` (line 1488) requires it; when false the call goes to `driver.find` plus `applyInMemoryAggregation`, filtered measures included.
- "so does one under a non-UTC `timezone`, unless the driver declares `supports.zonedDateBucketing` … and the zone resolves to an area/location" — true. `zoneNative` (lines 1457–1458) is `utc`, or `area` together with `supports.zonedDateBucketing === true`; `tzRequiresInMemory` is its negation and gates `nativeAggregate`. "non-UTC" is the right word: `judgeBucketZone` sends `Etc/UTC`, `GMT`, `Zulu` down the UTC path on every driver. "resolves to" is the right verb: the engine judges the runtime's resolved name, so `CST` (resolved to `America/Chicago`) is pushed down although the raw string has no slash; the sentence does not claim otherwise.
- "PostgreSQL via `driver-sql`" — true for every dialect. `sql-driver.ts:409` is `zonedDateBucketing: this.isPostgres`; MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle and SQLite get `false`, and Turso inherits `false`. No other driver package declares the bit (grep of `packages/` at the head: the only declaring site is that line). The driver's own second wall agrees: `aggregate` refuses a zone on a non-PostgreSQL dialect and `buildDateBucketExpr` answers `null` for it.
- "`Asia/Taipei` buckets in the database" — true on PostgreSQL: `(col)::timestamptz AT TIME ZONE ?` with the resolved zone bound. Within the note this also carries the filtered measure down, because `driver-sql` declares `aggregationFilter: true` on every dialect. One refinement the sentence does not need to carry: a `Field.date` column is pushed down too but is never zone-shifted, on either path, so the answer is the same.
- "`+08:00` or `EST5EDT` never" — true as the engine defines it. Both resolve to a name with no `/` (or do not resolve), which `judgeBucketZone` classes as `memory` before any driver capability is read, so no driver changes the outcome. This rests on the runtime's zone resolution, not on the driver; it is pinned at the repo's Node floor by `engine-aggregate-timezone.test.ts:177` (`EST5EDT`, `+08:00`, `Bogus/Zone`), so a runtime that started resolving `EST5EDT` to an area name would fail that test before the skill went stale. Holds.
- Other sentences: `SKILL.md` lines 25–26 and 43 list `timezone` as legal on `aggregate` "for date bucketing" and say nothing about where it runs; the Date-Bucketed Grouping section does not mention `timezone`. No other skill under `skills/` repeats the old claim. The rewrite is complete for the card.
- Against the card: the Change paragraph asks for "a driver declaring `supports.zonedDateBucketing` … buckets a zoned date in the database; on every other driver … in memory". The text adds the area/location condition, which the card omitted and the code requires. That addition is correct and necessary: without it the skill would promise a database bucket for `+08:00` on PostgreSQL.

**`skills/objectstack-query/evals/filters-pagination-search.json`**, case 9:

- `expected_output` is true sentence by sentence: the call shape is the one the skill teaches (`groupBy` item with `dateGranularity`, a `count` with a per-measure `filter`, `timezone` in the aggregate bag); PostgreSQL pushes the zoned bucket and the filtered count down; SQLite declares no zoned bucketing and keeps the whole call in memory; `+08:00` stays in memory on every driver. The prompt exercises both conditions of the new sentence (driver and zone form), which is what the card asks.
- The grader is literal: `packages/qa/scenarios/README.md` states tokens match as case-sensitive substrings and no model judges an answer. Judged against that grader:

S1 (should-fix) — `must_not_contain` holds `"timezone: '+08:00'"`, while the prompt itself asks "What changes if I pass the zone as `+08:00`?". A correct answer that restates the asked variant as code ("with `timezone: '+08:00'` the whole call runs in memory, on PostgreSQL too") is graded FAIL, although it says exactly what the rule text says. The rule never forbids writing that spelling; it says the spelling never buckets in the database. The token therefore tests something the text does not say and punishes the answer the prompt invites, so the with-skill pass rate for this case under-reads for a reason unrelated to the skill. Fix on the eval file alone: drop that token (the `must_contain` pair `timezone: 'Asia/Taipei'` and `in memory` already separate a right answer from one that recommends the offset), or reword the prompt so the offset form is not something the answer is asked to discuss. No other case in the file forbids a string its own prompt asks about.

- N1 (nit) — `must_contain` requires the identifier `zonedDateBucketing` and the exact phrases `in the database` and `in memory`. An answer that is right in substance but says "pushed down to SQL" or does not name the capability fails. This is in line with the file's precedent (`keyset`, `stored`) and uses the skill's own wording, so it is accepted as is.
- N2 (nit) — `must_not_contain` `date_trunc` guards against a raw-SQL answer. The PostgreSQL arm does not use `date_trunc` (it labels with `to_char` over `AT TIME ZONE`), so an answer naming it would be inaccurate anyway. Accepted as is.

No must-fix. One should-fix, S1, open on this head: it earns a delta review of its fix, and the text in `rules/aggregation.md` needs no change.

- `rules/aggregation.md` and `.changeset/34597-skills-zoned-date-bucket.md` are untouched by the delta, so every clause-by-clause judgment of the earlier record on the skill sentence carries over unchanged. The net diff against `main` is still three files, +25/-2, nothing in `packages/**`. Right.
- `main` moved (now `6d2db1d7ef`) but no commit between the merge-base and it touches `skills/objectstack-query/**`, `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` or `sql-driver.ts`, so the code the sentence was judged against is the code on `main` today.

Unchanged by the delta. `@objectstack/skills` patch for published skill text and one eval case is right; `Check Changeset` completed `success` on this head. The changeset prose describes the sentence and the eval case, not the removed token, so it still agrees with the tree.

Clause-②: no — on the PR body and in the changeset, and correct: no runtime behaviour changes, nothing is removed or narrowed. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions` 1 (authored at `TIER_DEFAULT` under a contract-review mandate for `skills/**`): answered as before, by the at-tier review of the authored text, now on this head as well.
- Out-of-scope finding (`content/docs/data-modeling/queries.mdx` on a structured `groupBy` alias against the skill's "column keys" wording): still "noted, not filed" on the PR body. Outside both `hits` and the diff, not judged here; the earlier ask stands, that the seat file it or state why not.
- The fix round raises no new flag and no new `open_questions` entry.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no code in the diff, so no new id materialisation or in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

**`skills/objectstack-query/evals/filters-pagination-search.json`**, case 9 at this head:

- S1: closed. The token `timezone: '+08:00'` is gone from `must_not_contain`. The prompt asks "What changes if I pass the zone as `+08:00`?", and an answer that restates the asked variant as code and says it keeps the whole call in memory is no longer graded FAIL by the literal substring grader.

The removed token never caught the one wrong claim that matters ("`+08:00` buckets in the database on PostgreSQL") unless it happened to be spelled as that exact code fragment, and no substring token can catch it; so the case's discriminating power is what it was, minus a false negative.

**`skills/objectstack-query/rules/aggregation.md`**: untouched by the delta; the earlier clause-by-clause judgment holds on this head.

Earlier nits, both accepted as is on the earlier record and unchanged here: the `must_contain` phrasing is literal (`zonedDateBucketing`, `in the database`, `in memory`), in line with the file's precedent and the skill's own wording; and `date_trunc` in `must_not_contain` guards a raw-SQL answer that would be inaccurate anyway. No must-fix, no should-fix.
